transcript:
Recording header: 2026-10-06 15:00 UTC
Duration 54m; Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Dr. Alan Mercer (CISO, Riverview), Sasha Kim (Head of IT), Leo Rivera (Eng Manager)
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we really appreciate the time. This is Maya, I'm the AE on the account, Jordan's our SE. Quick agenda: SOC 2/ISO posture, trust center access, controls mapping, and any KMS / data residency questions.
[00:15] Dr. Mercer: Thanks. We've got some specific auditor asks around data residency and KMS for our patient PII, and want to see how your SOC 2 scope maps to our control set, especially for ISO alignment.
[00:28] Maya: Totally. Jordan, do you want to kick off with the reports we can share?
[00:33] Jordan: Sure. We can provide the SOC 2 Type II report, typically it's the full report under NDA, plus our ISO 27001 cert summary and a controls mapping artifact. We host a Trust Center where customers can request access to the bundle, and we can add Riverview's security contact there. Sorry, Trust Center was miss-typed earlier; it's the access portal.
[00:50] Sasha: When you say full report under NDA, is that the actual testing evidence or just the attestation letter? Our compliance team usually needs the testwork detail for mapping.
[00:59] Jordan: Good question. We provide the SOC 2 Type II report and the related testing summary. For raw testwork we typically provide redacted evidence under an NDA or through our portal where we control distribution. We'll confirm what level of detail we can share; it depends on legal and third-party constraints.
[01:15] Leo: And for the controls mapping, can you give a sample? We want to align your control IDs to our ISO 27001 annex A controls and our internal policies.
[01:24] Jordan: Yep, we maintain a controls mapping spreadsheet that maps SOC 2 controls and ISO clauses to Redwood product controls and operational procedures. We'll share that as a spreadsheet (that's what we recommended).
[01:35] [01:35] Maya: Alan, can you describe any hard requirements around key management? Are you trying to require customer-managed KMS for all workloads?
[01:45] Dr. Mercer: Ideally yes for production PII datasets. We need BYOK or customer-managed keys in a KMS/HSM. Also we have residency constraints; certain datasets must remain in EU or in our private cloud.
[01:58] Jordan: For our hosted offering, we support provider-managed keys by default, and we have options for customer-managed keys in supported clouds. For Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments, customers can integrate with their KMS or HSM, that's standard. There is some engineering coordination for key rotation and access proofs.
[02:15] Sasha: Is that the same for audit logs? We need continuous export of audit logs to our SIEM and at least 7 years of retention for certain events.
[02:26] Jordan: Audit logs: we provide tenant-scoped audit logs with event detail (who/what/when). For hosted customers, logs can be streamed to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3 export with encryption. Retention in the Trust Center is default 90 days, but we offer add-on retention plans and can arrange long-term storage exports. For private deployments you control retention locally.
[02:45] [02:45] Dr. Mercer: What about RBAC & SSO? We use SAML-based SSO and need SCIM provisioning plus role separation so developers don't get production keys.
[02:56] Maya: We support SSO via SAML and OIDC, and SCIM provisioning for user sync. Role-based access control is supported with customizable roles and fine-grained permissions. Jordan, maybe mention session tokens and token expiry defaults?
[03:08] Jordan: Sure, default session tokens are configurable; we support short-lived API tokens, per-route permissions, and administrative audit records. You can segment by project/org and apply least privilege. There have been instances where SCIM mapping needs a little tweak if customer has custom attributes, Jordan chuckles, but it's straightforward.
[03:26] Leo: Any third-party subservice concerns? Our auditors want to see list of subproc vendors.
[03:31] Jordan: Our SOC 2 includes vendor management and lists key subprocessors. We'll include the subproc list in the Trust Center export and call out things like our cloud infra provider, logging provider etc.
[03:45] Sasha: Data residency: If we need EU-only, does Redwood provide region isolation for hosted?
[03:52] Jordan: Yes, we have region-specific deployments and can route data to EU regions. For stricter guarantees you can opt for Redwood Dedicated or Private for physical isolation. Note that dedicated capacity has contractual SLAs and capacity commitment.
[04:10] [04:10] Dr. Mercer: How about encryption at rest and in transit? Is it AES-256? TLS 1.2/1.3?
[04:18] Jordan: We use TLS 1.2+ (TLS 1.3 preferred) for transit, and AES-256 for at-rest encryption. For customer keys we integrate with KMS APIs (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM-backed keys if required. We'll provide architecture notes on envelope encryption and key rotation policies.
[04:40] Maya: There's a common question about model caching and KV cache if you're using hosted inference, do any model caches persist PII?
[04:49] Jordan: Good callout. Our KV/prefix caching is transient and designed not to persist PII; by default we scrub sensitive fields and have cache TTLs. For regulated workloads we recommend private deployments with guaranteed isolation and configurable cache behavior.
[05:05] Sasha: Can you scope the SOC 2 to only include the inference service or is it broader? We only need certain components in scope for our auditors.
[05:12] Jordan: The SOC scope typically covers the hosted API surface plus underlying infra components. For Private deployments, the scope is different; there we can provide attestation on the control implementation we manage vs. customer-managed portions. We can discuss scoping options with your auditor.
[05:30] [05:30] Maya: Quick note on legal: some customers need a data processing agreement (DPA) and standard contractual clauses for EU; we have templates and we can start that process.
[05:40] Dr. Mercer: Yes, DPA plus SCCs are necessary. Also, any pen test evidence?
[05:47] Jordan: We do annual penetration tests and can provide high-level summaries. Full reports often require NDA but we can share executive summaries and remediation timelines.
[06:00] Leo: Operational questions — how fast can you spin up a private deployment or dedicated capacity? We're thinking pilot in Q4.
[06:08] Maya: For Dedicated we typically do a capacity and contract lead time; for small pilots it's a few weeks; for full dedicated clusters it can be months based on capacity. Private on-prem is longer; depends on infra. We'll sketch options in the follow-up.
[06:25] [06:25] Sasha: For KMS integration specifically, we need to see key rotation logs and separation of duties around key admin.
[06:33] Jordan: We'll capture those controls in the mapping sheet — key rotation cadence, who can request rotations, audit trails in KMS, and how access is granted. For customer-managed KMS, key admins live in the customer org. For provider-managed keys, we enforce strict access and rotation policies and provide rotation artifacts.
[06:52] Dr. Mercer: Could you share an example mapping to ISO 27001 Annex A? That's high priority.
[06:57] Jordan: Yes, the controls mapping spreadsheet includes ISO clause mappings and control owners; we'll give you a version redacted for public consumption and a fuller one under NDA.
[07:10] [07:10] Maya: We're going to put together a deliverable: SOC 2 Type II report (or Trust Center access), controls mapping spreadsheet, KMS integration notes, and a proposed timeline for a pilot. Is that aligned?
[07:18] Dr. Mercer: Yes. Also please include the subprocessor list and pen test summary.
[07:22] Maya: Noted.
[07:25] [07:25] Jordan: Just to manage expectations — some artifacts require an NDA and legal approval. We'll start the process immediately.
[07:32] Sasha: One more question on logs — can we get immutable logs or tamper-evident storage? Our auditors asked about integrity guarantees.
[07:41] Jordan: We can provide write-once storage export, and we support signed logs for tamper evidence. For hosted service we use S3 with object lock option for long-term retention exports; for private deployments you can implement your own immutability patterns.
[07:58] [07:58] Dr. Mercer: Okay that's helpful. Any performance tradeoffs for encryption or using customer-managed keys?
[08:05] Jordan: There's typically a negligible latency increase for envelope encryption and KMS calls, but it's small relative to overall inference time; if you expect microsecond latency requirements we can discuss optimized paths — otherwise it's usually fine.
[08:21] Maya: We'll flag that for the pilot benchmarks — Jordan can run a latency test with customer-managed keys in a staging env.
[08:30] Leo: For the controls mapping, can you indicate which controls are fully Redwood-managed, which are shared responsibility, and which are customer-managed? That's critical.
[08:40] Jordan: Absolutely — the spreadsheet has columns for control, implementation owner (Redwood/Customer/Shared), evidence location, and references to SOC sections.
[08:52] [08:52] Sasha: Regarding SSO provisioning, does Redwood support attribute-based access controls or just role mapping?
[08:59] Jordan: We support role mapping and can accept custom attributes for ABAC-style enforcement in the product via policy engine; setup can require a small engineering step if you need non-standard attributes.
[09:10] Maya: any other auditor asks we should be aware of?
[09:14] Dr. Mercer: They want assurance that logs related to data access are searchable and exportable on demand and that we can produce access histories for individuals.
[09:24] Jordan: We have audit endpoints and can generate search exports; retention constraints apply but we can export historical logs for legal discovery as part of the add-on retention.
[09:34] [09:34] Maya: OK, let's recap next steps — we'll send the SOC 2 Type II report link and Trust Center access request, Jordan will attach the controls mapping sheet and KMS notes, and we'll propose times for a KMS deep dive and a pilot plan.
[09:50] Dr. Mercer: That works. Thanks both.
[09:55] Sasha: Thanks.
[09:58] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and Slack, and include the legal/engineering contacts.
[10:03] [10:03] Recording end.
Notes on transcription: occasional mistaken words (Trust Center noted as Trust Centre earlier), minor overlap and speaker label jitter.
